title: Compositional Generalisation for Explainable Hate Speech Detection
measurement_description: Detection of hate speech and stereotypes against religious groups, specifically using the Muslim community as an example of a group targeted by specific derogatory comparisons.
findings: The paper uses the Muslim community as a primary example to illustrate that hate speech detection models struggle with compositional generalization. For instance, models may learn that a derogatory comparison like 'are terrorists' is hateful only when associated with Muslims, as seen in biased training data, and fail to generalize its hateful nature when applied to other targets. The paper's proposed method of training on balanced synthetic data helps models disentangle these correlations and improve generalization, although specific results for religious groups are not isolated.
